what: Tradeweb runs electronic marketplaces for bonds and other fixed income products. Institutions that used to trade government bonds, corporate bonds and interest rate swaps by telephone now do it on its platforms.
customers: Asset managers, hedge funds, insurers, central banks, banks and retail brokerages, more than 3,000 clients in total.
money: government bonds, mortgage-backed securities and swaps
Money markets, equities and market data
moat: Liquidity that attracts more liquidity: once enough dealers and buyers quote on a platform, trading moves there and stays.
risks: Trading volumes fall in quiet markets
Analyst targets imply the shares are already fully valued
Competition for electronic corporate bond trading is intense
Pricing per trade falls as volumes migrate to electronic venues
opportunities: Revenue grew about 19% last year and about 20% a year over three years
Operating margin of 41% with cash of $2.1 billion and almost no debt
Fixed income trading is still far less electronic than equities, so the shift has years to run
watch: Average daily volume by asset class and the revenue capture per million traded.
